preview: Sarah: Straight up: the only Bitcoin miner we stock under 100 W is that Thor X1 at ~25 W — and you've ruled out Hammer. Everything else in SHA-256 starts around 100 W.

messages.text: Help me pick
Happy to. Two quick things: is this your first miner, and what do you pay for power roughly?
no, second miner. my. price is 0.30c per kilowatt
Ran the power-cost calculator · 30¢/kWh
Read the magic miner 40t page

At 30¢ a kWh, size matters more than usual. The Magic Miner 40T ($799, 40 TH/s) runs ~650 W — about $140 a month — or 30 TH/s in Eco at 450 W, closer to $97. It's our best value per terahash, Ships November 21, 2026.

What are you already running, and is this going on a desk or in a garage?
desk. I want something in the ~50watt range
Read the nexus s1 10th s page
Searched the catalog · NerdQaxe Bitaxe low power desktop miner

Closest to that is the Hammer Thor X1: 3.2 TH/s at ~25 W, $219, in stock. At your 30¢ that's about $5 a month to run. Note it ships without a PSU — it's USB-C powered.

Next step up is the BC04, 6 TH/s at ~100 W, $239, about $22 a month.

Which way — lowest draw, or double the hashrate?
I want ethernet port and power supply included

Then it's the BC04: 6 TH/s, ~100 W, ethernet plus WiFi, and the 120 W power supply and cord are in the box. $239, in stock, ships within 5 business days with the plug matched to your address.

About $22 a month at 30¢. Want me to build the cart?
too may watts.I also hate how hammer miners look. Green/white is hideous
Searched the catalog · Bitaxe Gamma low watt miner ethernet

Straight answer: nothing outside Hammer hits all three. The NerdQX (8 TH/s, ~145 W, $299, PSU included, black) is the best-looking small unit we have, but it's WiFi only.

So one wish has to give. Is ethernet a hard requirement, or can you live with WiFi and get the looks?
sure

Good. The NerdQX it is — 8 TH/s, ~145 W (about $31 a month at 30¢), ~40 dB, PSU included.

One thing before I build it: the US cable version is out of stock right now; EU and UK are live. Which are you shipping to?
too many watts. I need something smaller
Searched the catalog · Bitaxe

Straight up: the only Bitcoin miner we stock under 100 W is that Thor X1 at ~25 W — and you've ruled out Hammer. Everything else in SHA-256 starts around 100 W.

So it's a real trade-off: the X1's draw, or a NerdQX at 145 W. Which matters more to you, the watts or the brand?
